heading: Six families, some unplaced households, and a lot of namesakes
lead: This site has been counting badly. It said «seven lines», then «eight», and listed Senj beside Carnia as though they were the same kind of thing — when Senj is a place our own family reached and Carnia is where it started. Three different things were being added together. They are separated here, and the count only applies to the first of them — which now runs to six, because Corsica has earned a lane of its own and Vodnjan has earned one by being read.

why.text: Four households of the surname can be traced to a place they came *from*, and they came from three different directions for three different reasons. Three are documented; the fourth is family lore. **These are the only things this archive calls families**, and nothing joins any two of them.

why.lab: A station is not a family
why.text: Gologorica, Gračišće, Crikvenica, Senj, Pfullingen are **stops on one road** — our road — not separate lines. So are Perinuša and Opačac on the Venetian road, and Umag, Brtonigla and Koper on the Cretan one. They have pages because there is a lot to say about each; they are not additions to the count.

why.lab: And a line can run beside ours without being ours
why.text: **Corsica is the clearest case, and it is now drawn as a line rather than buried in a footnote.** It has everything the other four have — a place, a first generation with dates, six documented generations, a route out and a diaspora — and it has no connection to Istria whatever. That is exactly why it is worth drawing. A reader who finds a Franceschi in Puerto Rico or Caracas should be able to see, on the same picture, that there is a fully documented family of the name that goes there and is not this one.

why.lab: And a namesake is not a relative
why.text: *De Franceschi* means only «of the Franceschi» — the household of a man called Francesco. It was invented independently wherever an Italian-speaking clerk had two Francescos to tell apart. So a De Franceschi in Corsica or Bologna or Rio Grande do Sul is not evidence of anything at all until a document joins them, and this archive will not pretend otherwise.

families.name: Out of Carnia, for work
families.from: The Val di Gorto above Ovaro, in Friuli
families.rests: A De Franceschi of Mione on the 1679 headmen's list, working in the County of Pazin; the surname in the Moncalvo di Pisino baptism book from 1661; ANNO · DOMNI · 1711 cut over the house at Gologorica; and an unbroken register descent at Gračišće from 1787.
families.who: This archive's own family, and Carlo and Camillo De Franceschi's.

families.name: Out of Venice, as soldiers
families.from: Venice, by way of Zadar and Omiš
families.rests: Louis I's privilege of 1359; the foundation plaque of Francesco the Venetian at Omiš dated 18 June 1584; Provveditore Mocenigo's donation charter of 1717; the Imotski death register of 1845, where a Franceschi born at Omiš dies at Imotski.
families.who: Zuane, who took Imotski in 1717, and the mills at Perinuša.

families.name: Out of Crete, as refugees
families.from: Candia, by way of Zante and Šibenik
families.rests: The Venetian war pension of 1674, still being drawn at Capodistria in 1730; Chrysoula Marulli, a Cretan wife married in 1727; and the estate at Seget bought in 1720 with 1724 on its portal and 1732 on its cistern. The flight itself is tradition, well supported.
families.who: The Seget and Umag house, nobles of Capodistria from 1802.

families.name: Southern Istria — Pula, Fažana, Ližnjan
families.from: Unknown — but a Friulian trace at Zoppola
families.rests: Thirty-one people in the family's own tree, in the Pula and Fažana registers from **1667** and at Ližnjan into the twentieth century. **This is now known to be the tail of a larger southern-Istrian household rather than an origin of its own**, and the question is which of the other three it belongs to. The one clue that pointed at Friuli was tested in September 2026 and proved to be a mis-attached record from a Zoppola family of the same name.
families.who: Grgo of Ližnjan, an Antonio in the naval cemetery at Pula, and two who died in France.

families.name: Out of Corsica, to the Caribbean
families.rests: A family history written from inside it: **«LOS FRANCESCHI, la pequeña historia de una familia»**, Napoleón Franceschi González, Caracas 2002. **Pietro Franceschi, 29 June 1694 – 12 February 1771**, then Gasparo (1721–99), Francesco Maria (1750–1828), Pietro (1789–1871) and **Simone, born and dead at Ersa, 1826–1907**, whose son François Marie died at Miranda in Venezuela in 1918. Ninety pages, and **not one line of it touches Istria.**
families.who: A dry, poor cape that never held two thousand people, so they went to sea or they left.

clusters_head: Households of the name that must belong to one of the four, and cannot yet be assigned
clusters_lead: These were being counted as lines. They are not origins; they are real households in real registers whose parent family this archive cannot yet name. Each one is a question with an address.

clusters.what: Kobler, working the civic registers, found three and declined to join them to each other. **Valentino, «venuto dalla Carnia», a citizen in 1739** — almost certainly the Carnian family. **Giovanni Battista, «venuto da Pisino», a citizen in 1746** — almost certainly the same, since «da Pisino» in a Fiume register means the county, and that is where Gologorica is. And an earlier Fiume stock that is nobody's yet.

Kandler's list of the Carnian families settled at Sanvincenti names Defranceschi among Lupieri, Fiorencis, Fabris, Crosilla and the rest. So the origin is Carnian; whether it is *our* Carnian household or another out of the same valley is not settled.

A citizen-class household from before 1772 — Dominus Giovanni Battista, son of Dominus Francesco, marrying Catharina Akačić by dispensation. Styled *Dominus*, which separates them from the peasants on the same page. Which of the four they belong to is open.

**Read, September 2026.** Not a scatter but one family: in the Pula registers from **1667**, then Pula, Fažana, Premantura, Medulin and Barban for three centuries, with Ližnjan as its last address rather than its origin — which means **Ližnjan is not a separate family and should not be counted as one**. Two outliers complicate it: a death at Rovinj in 1728, a baptism at Šterna in 1778. **The one clue that pointed north has been tested and discarded**: the Giambattista with children at Zoppola in Udine is a local man «De Franceschi o Samassa» of a local Zoppola family, attached by Smart Matching — and Zoppola is the Friulian plain, not Carnia. The cluster has no origin yet.

A third and much larger southern presence, and Carlo's own book names Franceschi among the nobles of Pola «venuti da Capodistria» before the plague of 1631 — which would make them the extinct Koper family, not any of the four.

dest_head: Where the name went — and whose name it was
dest_lead: Every destination on the family's old map, with the one thing the map did not say: which family it belongs to, and how well that is known. Half of them are not this family at all, and saying so is the point.

dests.what: Zdravko, Petar, Ivan and Felix in the labour camps and then the displaced-persons files, 1941–51. Named individuals, dated documents.
«Emigré Australie le 8.3.49» on Anton's index card. Zdravko's bronze at Horsham.
Hedviga Blažević died at Johannesburg in 2001; the keeper of this archive was born there.
Not a line — a station. Ivan went home to Senj and is buried there, 1925–1995.
Basilio of Gračišće, born 29 September 1909, and his son Dario born at Gallignana in 1937; Giuseppe born at Gračišće 1892, dead in New York 1940; Albina off the Conte Rosso in 1922.
Acta Croatica counts about sixty people of the name in Croatia today, mostly born at Split or Imotski. That is the Dalmatian family, still there.
Seget's own country. Koper is a title rather than a home: nobles of Capodistria from 1802, while living at Seget.

Grga died at Zagreb and thirteen graves of the name are in the city's cemeteries. **Monheim, corrected**: the pin's coordinates point at Bavaria, but the town that matters is Monheim am Rhein — and the only private listing of «Defranceski» in the whole German directory is five kilometres away at Langenfeld, in the same district. Not proof, and the people are living, so no one is named. But the pin is no longer sourceless.

Rotilio, eighth of the Eleven of Gračišće, is said to have gone to Buenos Aires with two daughters. **Searched properly in September 2026 and not found**: no Rotilio of this surname anywhere in the Argentine record, and the Defranceschi who are there are an Italian-mainland stock. The album's one supporting detail — the name of his wife — turns out to be his sister's marriage. CEMLA's arrival index is behind a bot check and stays unsearched.

dests.place: Brazil — Rio Grande do Sul, Santa Catarina, São Paulo
dests.what: The largest cluster of the surname anywhere, and **not this family**. The in-law names are Marcato, Busatto, Poletta, Raminelli, Barbiero, Negri, Catteri, Facco — every one of them Veneto. This is the Italian colonisation from 1875 out of the Veneto, Friuli and the Valsugana, with a separate São Paulo coffee-belt migration beside it.
Domme De Franceski, born in Italy 1880, at the Penn Iron Mining Company at Norway, Michigan, with a wife born in Switzerland. Nothing joins him to Istria.
Italian-speaking Switzerland, over the border from Lombardy. A different stock of the same ordinary patronymic.

**Now a line of its own on this page.** A Florentine-descended family settled at **Ersa in Cap Corse**, documented from **1694** in Napoleón Franceschi's own history of it, out through Puerto Rico, Saint Thomas, Trinidad and Haiti to Venezuela. It produced a Napoleonic brigadier general, made a baron of the Empire in 1810, and a modern historian of the Revolution. It has nothing to do with Istria, and that is the point of drawing it.
Two born at Barban in 1924 and 1931, dead at Charleville in the Moselle in 2002 and at Cannes in 2016. The Istrian exodus took a road this archive had not recorded.

dests.place: Venezuela · Puerto Rico · Trinidad · St Thomas
dests.what: The Corsican family's own road, out of Ersa through the French and Spanish Caribbean. There is a *Centro de Arte Alejandro Franceschi* at Yauco in Puerto Rico and a village there called **Córcega**. Not this family — and fully documented, which is what makes it useful.

close: So the honest sentence is this. **Six families with an origin in documents, of which five are documented and one — Ližnjan, now folded into southern Istria — has only a place.** The sixth is **Vodnjan**, added on 10 September 2026: twelve households in a 1945 cadastre, then five generations read by eye out of a marriage register that no index anywhere contains. **Three of the six are ours or arrived beside ours; one, Corsica, never came near Istria at all and is drawn to show what a parallel line looks like.** Four clusters of real households belong to one of them and cannot yet be told which — Fiume, Svetvinčenat, Bakar and now **Rovinj**, which holds the earliest dated Istrian record of the name. And a diaspora in which five destinations are demonstrably ours, four belong to the other families, and the rest are people who share the commonest patronymic in Italy.
source_fam: Assembled September 2026 from this archive's own pages, and restructured after David Defranceski pointed out that it had been adding three different kinds of thing together and calling the total «lines».

svetjoin.heading: Svetvinčenat, 1657–1737 — and the «Pula 1667» that was never Pula
svetjoin.lead: David asked for the people in the roster to be worked through one by one, to see whether any of them join two regions. This is the first result, and it moves a line. It came out of the three earliest people in the roster — born 1669, 1671 and 1674 — by asking the only question that matters about an index entry: **which book is it actually in?**

rows.lab: How the parish was identified
rows.text:
The index gives the place of these baptisms as «**Croazia, Austria**» — no parish at all, which is why they have sat unplaced. But every FamilySearch index entry carries the ark of the image it was read from, and every image ark resolves to a **DGS film number**. These resolve to **DGS 005497884**, and the catalogue entry for that film reads: «**Matična knjiga, 1568–1917 · Rimokatolička crkva. Župa Svetvinčenat**» — the parish register of **Svetvinčenat**, held by the Croatian State Archive in Zagreb.

So the register is named even though the index is not. **The method is repeatable and it is now the archive's standard practice for any «Croazia, Austria» entry.**

rows.lab: Which corrects the fourth line
rows.text:
This archive's fourth family opens: «**Pula, 1667** — Anto De Franceschi, with children entered in October 1667 and November 1669 — the earliest of the cluster.» Those are **Franceschina, baptised 23 October 1667**, and **Mattia, born 8 November 1669** — both children of **Anto De Franceschi and Marta**.

They are not Pula entries. **They are Svetvinčenat entries**, forty kilometres north, in a different parish and a different world. The southern-Istrian line's earliest evidence has been standing on a place-name the index never gave it.

rows.lab: And Svetvinčenat is the Carnian colony
rows.text:
That matters because Svetvinčenat is not an unknown. It is the cluster this archive lists as **not placed** — one hundred and forty-two records from 1666 — and three separate authorities call it Carnian. **Kandler** names the Carnian families settled at Sanvincenti. **Doblanović**, reading the Status animarum of 1734, finds the surnames that occur inside the *castello* and nowhere else in the parish — «**De Franceschi, Crosila, Bergamo, Moro, Fiorencis**» — and says they «came from the area of Carnia» and were «mainly in trade». **Brhan** finds a **Stanzia De Franceschi** on the 1820 cadastral map, a farmstead the family had held and already lost.

**So the oldest records of the «origin unknown» line are records of a documented Carnian colony.**

rows.lab: Twelve households, eighty years
rows.text:
Pulled out of the index and sorted, the parish gives a continuous presence:

**1657** Francesco, son of **Zuanne and Orsola** · **1666** Colotta, daughter of **Nadal and Fiora** · **1666** Fioretta, daughter of **M.ro Batta and Domenica** · **1667** Franceschina and **1674** Mattio, of **Anto and Marta** · **1670** Luca, of **Francesco and Giacoma** · **1671** Giacomo, of **Andrea and Zuana** · **1673** Giovanna and **1688** Zuana, of **Gaspero, with Marietta then Anta** · **1701** Veneranda, of **Gasparo and Antonia** · **1703** Domenica, of **Piero and Vittoria** · **1704** Antonio, of **Mattio and Zuanna** · **1707** Piero, of **Lunardo and Eufemia** · **1709** Maria, of **Nardo and Zuanna** · **1722** Martino, of **Mattio and Elisabetta** · **1733** Maria, of **Giacomo and Anzoletta** · **1734** Pietro and **1735** Bata, of **Nadal and Anta** · **1737** Andrea, of **Vitorio and Francesca**.

That is **at least twelve distinct fathers of this surname in one small town between 1657 and 1737** — and the earliest of them, Zuanne, is **four years before the surname enters the Moncalvo book** and twelve years before the Mione headmen's list.

rows.lab: Two given names that reach out of it
rows.text: **Lunardo — Nardo — Leonardo.** A Leonardo De Franceschi is baptising children at Svetvinčenat in 1707 and 1709. The Gologorica house's own byname is «**detti Leonardi**», and its pedigree carries Leonardus 1697–1773, Leonardus 1766–1848 and Leonardus 1847–1917. Leonardo is not a common name in these registers, and it is now in both places at once. Inferred **Vitorio.** A Vitorio De Franceschi is baptising at Svetvinčenat in 1737 — and Vitorio, Vittorio and Victorius run right through the Pula–Fažana–Medulin group: Vitorio born 1720, Vitorio 1758, Vittorio 1795, Vittorio Giovanni 1849. **Neither is proof.** A shared font-name is the weakest evidence there is, and this archive has said so about better cases than this. What they are is **two threads to pull**, both bounded: the Svetvinčenat register is filmed and readable, and it will say whether these are the same men.

rows.lab: What this changes, stated carefully
rows.text:
The Lines page draws the fourth family as «**Out of southern Istria — origin unknown**», documented from 1667 at Pula. Two of those three words now need work. The **1667** is right; the **Pula** is wrong; and **«origin unknown» may not survive**, because the register those earliest entries come from is a parish whose De Franceschi are called Carnian by everyone who has studied them.

What this archive will **not** do is redraw the diagram on this. Two of the twelve Svetvinčenat fathers could be the ancestors of the Pula group, or none of them could; the town sat on the road between the county of Pazin and the Pula country and people moved both ways. The lane keeps its dotted origin, the correction to «Pula» is made, and the Svetvinčenat cluster is now the **first place this archive will read page by page** rather than by index.

svetjoin.source_svet: FamilySearch record index, collection 2040054, Croatia church books — personas resolved to image arks, image arks resolved through the digital-archive service to **DGS 005497884**, and that film identified in the FamilySearch catalogue as «Matična knjiga, 1568–1917», Rimokatolička crkva, Župa Svetvinčenat, Hrvatski državni arhiv u Zagrebu (catalogue item koha:728445). Read September 2026. The Carnian identification of the parish is Kandler by way of Carlo De Franceschi's «L'Istria» (1879), Danijela Doblanović on the Status animarum of 1734, and Dean Brhan on the Catasto franceschino of 1820.

svetread.heading: Reading the Svetvinčenat register, page by page
svetread.lead: The index gave twelve fathers. The register gives the family. These are the first openings read image by image off **DGS 005497884** — not searched, read — and they contain things no index will ever carry: who stood godparent, what the priest called them, and how that changed.

rows.lab: 20 May 1666 — the first sighting, and it is not a baptism of theirs
rows.text:
«Elena fig.la di Giacometta Redol, et di Cate sua mog.e, fu battezata da me D. Vicenzo Sines Can.co. **Comp.i furno M.ro Nadal de Franceschi**, et Elena mog.e di Sue Milicich.»

Five months before his own daughter is christened, **Nadal de Franceschi stands as godfather** at Svetvinčenat. Godparents are almost never indexed, which is exactly why the page had to be opened. And he is styled **M.ro — maestro**, a master craftsman.

rows.lab: 24 October 1666 — Colotta
rows.text: «**Colotta figlia di M.ro Nadal de Franceschi et di Fiora sua consorte**, nata li 10 d.o, et batt.a da me D. Vic.o; Comp.ri furno Giacometta Rebas, et Cata mog. di Dom.co Calcetta.» The name **Colotta** is written again in the margin, in the priest's own hand, the way this register indexes itself.

rows.lab: 22 November 1666 — Fioretta
rows.text: «**Fioretta figlia di M.ro Batta de Franceschi, et di Dom.ca sua cons.te**, nata li 18 d.o, et batt.a dal sud.o D. Pieu.o; Comp.ri furno **M.ro Matte Felicer**, et Dom.ca fig.la del q. **M.ro Franc.o Sovardo**.»

rows.lab: And the company they keep is the whole argument
rows.text:
Read the godparents across these two openings alone and the parish's Carnian colony assembles itself:

**M.ro Nadal de Franceschi** · **M.ro Zuanne Spinoti** · **M.ro Matte Fiorenza** · **M.ro Matte Felicer** · **il M.co Angelo Fabri, fattor** · M.ro Tomaso Selucer · M.ro Franc.o Sovardo.

**Spinotti. Fiorencis. Felice. Fabris.** Those are not four names that happen to be in a Croatian village in 1666. They are the Canale di Gorto — the same set that stands on the gravestones at Santa Maria di Gorto and on its war memorial, and the same set Doblanović finds inside this town's *castello* in the household book of 1734. **In 1666 they are all standing at each other's fonts**, and a De Franceschi is among them, called *maestro* like the rest.

rows.lab: 9 February 1674 — and now he is «il Signor»
rows.text:
Eight years later, same parish, same register:

«Vittoria fig.a di Giac.o Zebelin e di Elena sua leg.ma consorte… fu battezzata da me P. Fran.co Andreis Pievano. **Comp.ri furono il Sig.r Ant.o di Franceschi** e la Sig.ra Franceschetta Marchesi.»

And twelve days later, his own son:

«**Mattio figlio del Sig.r Ant.o di Franceschi e della Sig.ra Marta sua leg.ma consorte**, nato li 13 del sud.o mese, fu battezzato da me Pievano… **Comp.ri furono il Sig.r Conte Luciani** … et la Sig.ra Cattarina Pinco.»

**M.ro in 1666. Sig.r in 1674, with a Count for compare.** That is a household changing class inside eight years, written down by two priests who had no reason to flatter anybody. It is also the first time this archive has watched it happen to a De Franceschi anywhere.

**Refined, after reading further.** The change is not as clean as one opening made it look. As a *godparent* Anto is already «**il S.r**» on **20 October 1669** and again on **27 October 1669**; but in his own family's entry three weeks later, 11 November 1669, the priest still writes «**M.ro Ant.o**». The two styles run side by side through 1669, and it is by 1674 that *Sig.r* has won in both places. This archive published the tidier version first and is correcting it here rather than quietly.

rows.lab: What it is worth, and what it is not
rows.text:
It is worth this: the Svetvinčenat family was **Carnian, artisan, and rising**, and it was doing in the 1660s and 1670s exactly what the literature says the Carnians did — trade, credit, marriage inside the group, and then a title of respect. It sits beside the Gologorica house's own eighteenth-century business of lending money and buying up debts, and beside the Stanzia De Franceschi that Brhan finds on the 1820 cadastre and which had already passed out of the family.

**It does not join them.** Nothing read so far names a place of origin, and no entry ties any of these people to Mione, to Agrons, to Moncalvo or to Pula. Reading continues.

rows.lab: And the count has been chased
rows.text:
«**il Sig.r Conte Lucciani da [D/R]ignan**» — the word after *da* is a place and its first letter will not settle between a **D** and an **R**, enlarged five times. The surname will: it is **Lucciani**, with the double c, in a clear hand.

So who was he? The index carries a **Luciani** family baptising children in exactly these years — Bartolomio Zuane on 12 November 1674, Margherita Zuanna 1693, Maria Elena 1693, Matta 1682, Zuanne Domenigo 1684, Maria 1692. Resolved by film, every one of them is in the parish register of **Labin — Albona**, DGS 005494791 and 005494792, «Matična knjiga 1536–1910».

**The Luciani are an Albona house.** That is what the literature says too, and it is the family of the man who compiled the seventy-eight principal families of Albona. A count of theirs, standing at a De Franceschi font at Svetvinčenat in February 1674, is a man from the other side of Istria who had a reason to be there.

rows.lab: Which closes a circle across two hundred years
rows.text:
The name Luciani is already in this archive, twice, and neither time as a godparent.

**Carlo De Franceschi names him.** In *L'Istria: note storiche* (1879) Carlo thanks, among his sources, «Signori cav. **Tomaso Luciani** e Dr. **Antonio Scampicchio** di Albona» — the two Albona antiquaries he worked with.

**And their books are on his shelves.** The 2022 survey of the family library now in Zagreb finds, among the ex libris of previous owners, those of «**Tomaso Luciani of Labin**, the lawyer and politician **Antonio Scampicchio**, the historian **Pietro Kandler**». And Hauptmann, sorting the wrecked house at Gologorica in August 1945, lists among the manuscripts «**letters of Gabriele D'Annunzio, of Tomaso Luciani** and others».

So: a **Conte Lucciani of Albona** stands godfather to a De Franceschi child in 1674; a **Tomaso Luciani of Albona** is Carlo De Franceschi's collaborator in the 1870s, his letters are in the house, and his bookplate is in the library. **Two hundred years, one surname, one town, and no proved descent between them** — the archive states the pairing and stops there. But it is the sort of thing that stops being a coincidence when it happens three times.

rows.lab: The other count, still unexplained
rows.text:
This is the second count of consequence in these registers. The first is in this archive already, and he carries our own name.

«**Die 25 Martii 1720** … Bartholomeus filius legitimus **Domini Comitis Damiani de Franceschis** ac **Ursulae** eius coniugis, sacris undis renatus est» — the only occurrence of the surname in seventy-five years of the Gallignana baptism book, read leaf by leaf.

**Count Damian de Franceschis is in no source this archive holds.** He is not in the Blasonario's four families, not in Kobler's Fiume stocks, not in the Gologorica pedigree, and — checked now — **not in Carlo De Franceschi's own history of Istria**, whose index this archive has searched for him. A count of this surname in the County of Pazin in 1720, with a wife called Ursula and a son called Bartholomew, and nobody in two centuries of local historiography mentions him.

One small thing worth noting rather than claiming: the Svetvinčenat register's earliest De Franceschi couple, in 1657, are **Zuanne and Orsola** — Orsola being Ursula. It is a common name. It is also the second time this archive has met the pairing.

rows.lab: 25 October 1667 — and Anto is given a father
rows.text:
Two days after his own daughter is christened, Anto stands godfather again — and this time the priest writes him out in full:

«Gieppo fig.o leg.mo di M.ro Mattio Peleer e di Maria sua consorte, nato li 22 d.o, fu battezzato da me P. Fran.co Andreis Pievano. **Comp.ri furono M.ro Ant.o di Franceschi di Piero**, et Lucia moglie di Zuanne Bellauich da Barbana.»

«**di Piero**» is a patronymic, not a place. **Anto de Franceschi was the son of a Piero** — and that pushes the family at Svetvinčenat back a generation before any of the twelve fathers the index knows about, into a man born around the 1610s or 1620s. It is the single most useful line read so far, and no index carries it, because indexes do not transcribe godparents.

rows.lab: 23 October 1667 — Franceschina, and the company again
rows.text:
«**Franceschina fig.la leg.ma di M.ro Anto de Franceschi, et di Marta sua cons.te**, nata li 6 del sud.o, et batt.a da me D. Vic.o Pineo Can.co. Comp.ri furono **il Sig.r Angelo Ferri**, et la **Sig.ra Anna fig.la dell'Ill.mo s.r Nicolò Vieli**, moglie di Gieppo Cacheda.»

He is still **M.ro** here — but the godmother is already the daughter of an *Illustrissimo*. The climb this archive watched complete by 1674 has begun by 1667.

rows.lab: 20 and 27 October 1669 — asked twice in eight days
rows.text:
«Catarina fig.a di Sue Iacovich et d'Elena sua m.e… **Comp.ri furno il S.r Ant.o de Franceschi**, et Dom.ca mog. di Piero Bucich del Berro **di Due Castelli**.» — 20 October 1669.

«Zuanne fig.o di Michiel Bratolich et di Santa sua consorte… **Compari furono il S.r Ant.o de Franceschi**, et Zua mog. di Matte Reba.» — 27 October 1669.

Twice in eight days, for two unrelated households. **Anto de Franceschi is one of the men this parish asks.** Standing godparent was not a courtesy in a small Istrian town; it was a working relationship, and the register shows him in five of them in four years.

rows.lab: 11 November 1669 — Mattia, and she is a girl
rows.text:
«**Mattia fig.a del M.ro Ant.o de Franceschi e della S.ra Marta sua cons.te**, nata li 8 [del] sud.o mese, fu battezzata da me P. Fran.co Andreis Pievano. Comp.ri furono **il Sig.r Vicenzo Quelis**, e la Sig.ra Cattarina Piero.»

The index gives «Mattia De Franceschi, born 8 November 1669» without a sex. The register settles it: «**fig.a … nata**». **Mattia is a daughter**, not the son this archive had assumed from the name.

And the godfather is a **Quelis** — the same family that supplies «il s.r Vicenzo Quelis» in 1666 and «l'Ill.mo s.r Nicolò Vieli» in 1667. The Quelis stand for this family repeatedly, which is worth more than any single entry.

rows.lab: 11 January 1671 — and again, with no style at all
rows.text:
«Mattio fig.o di Michiel Bratolch e di Pasqua sua leg.ma consorte, nato li 6 d.o… **Comp.ri furono Ant.o di Franceschi**, e D.na Pasqua moglie di M.ro Mattio da Llosta.»

Here he is neither *M.ro* nor *S.r* — just Anto di Franceschi. The same priest, the same year. **The honorifics in this register are not a ladder; they are a habit that varies with the hand and the moment**, and this archive is recording that rather than building a story on it.

rows.lab: October 1671 — «et la Sig.ra Veneranda»
rows.text:
«**Comp.ri furono M.ro Ant.o de Franceschi**, et **la Sig.ra Veneranda** mog. del s.r Zuane de Cheri.»

Worth a note for a different reason. **Veneranda** is a name this family goes on using: a Veneranda de Franceschi is baptised here in **1701**, daughter of Gasparo; a **Veneranda Defranceschi née Subiotto** is in the record in **1837**; a **Veneranda Defranceschi née Demarin** later still. Here in 1671 it belongs to the woman standing beside Anto at the font. Font-names travel that way, and it is worth writing down where a family's names come *from*.

rows.lab: And a fifth Carnian surname walks in
rows.text:
Page 437, 10 June 1673: «Fran[cesco] fig.o di **Michiel Festa**, e d'Antonia sua legit.ma consorte». **Festa** is one of the families Brhan lists at **Gallignana** — «Gortan, **De Franceschi**, **Festa**, Picot, Baldè» — the Carnian households of the Pazin country. Here it is at Svetvinčenat, forty kilometres south, in 1673, in the same register as ours.

That now makes **Spinotti, Fiorencis, Felice, Fabris and Festa** all present in this one parish in these years — and every one of them is a name Brhan or Doblanović places in the Carnian migration, and three of them stand on the gravestones at Gorto.

rows.lab: 1 July 1688 — a daughter nobody knew about, and a death
rows.text:
«**Zuana figlia di M.ro Gaspero de Franceschi et d'Ant.a sua legg. consorte**… fu Batt.a da P. Piero Palin. **Compari furono M.ro Martin Ioancovich et Marina figlia del q. M.ro Batta de Franceschi.**»

Two new facts in one line of godparents. There is a **Marina de Franceschi**, adult in 1688 and therefore born by about 1670 — a daughter of the Batta whose child Fioretta was christened in 1666, and a person no index has. And «**del q.**» — *del quondam*, of the late — means **Batta de Franceschi was dead by July 1688**. A death this archive could not otherwise date at all.

rows.lab: 1692 and 1701 — the same woman, probably, and then her daughter
rows.text: In **October 1692** a «**D.a Marina moglie di M.ro Martin Francovich**» stands godmother; in **March 1701** the godmother at Gasparo's daughter's baptism is «**Maria figlia di Martin Francovich**». Set those beside 1688, where Marina de Franceschi stands *with* a M.ro Martin. Inferred **The likeliest reading is that Marina de Franceschi married Martin Francovich**, and that the Maria of 1701 is their daughter — which would make Batta's granddaughter the godmother at Gasparo's child's font, and tie two branches of this family together by choice rather than by guesswork. Two cautions, both real: the 1688 surname is written *Ioancovich* and the 1692 one *Francovich*, and standing as co-godparents does not make two people married. It is a reading, and it is labelled one.

rows.lab: 17 and 20 March 1701 — Gasparo, three days apart
rows.text:
«Giorgio figlio di Mico Matred e Zuana sua leg.ma consorte… fu hoggi batt. dal M.to R.do sig.r Can.co Pietro Quelis con lic.a mia. **Compari furono M.ro Gasp.e di Franceschi** e Cat.a moglie di Martin Bercovich.» — **17 March 1701**.

«**Veneranda figlia leg.ma di Gasparo de Franceschi et Antonia sua consorte**, nata li 12 d.o, fu hoggi batt.a dal M.to R.do sig.r Can.co Pietro Quelis di S. Vincenti. Comp.ri furono Zue de Blasio et Maria figlia di Martin Francovich.» — **20 March 1701**.

The same pattern as Nadal in 1666 and Anto in 1667: **a De Franceschi stands at somebody else's font days before his own child is carried to it.** Three generations of this family do it, in the same parish, across thirty-five years.

rows.lab: October 1692 — «M.ro Mattio de Franceschi»
rows.text:
A faded entry, and the word after the surname will not resolve: «Comp.ri furono **M.ro Mattio de Fran[ceschi]** de …, et Cata figlia del q. Zuane Lucian…» The Christian name and surname are clear enough. **Mattio de Franceschi is standing godfather in 1692** — and he is very likely the Mattio who fathers Antonio in 1704 and Martino in 1722.

The other godparent is «Cata, daughter of the late Zuane **Luciani**» — the Albona name again, this time as a resident of the parish.

rows.lab: 9 June 1702 — Leonardo, written out in full
rows.text:
«**Giacoma figlia leg.ma di M.ro Leonardo de Franceschi, et Eufemia sua leg.ma consorte**, nata li 30 d[el] passato, fu hoggi battezzata dal R.do P. D. Vicenzo Francas. Comp.ri furono Sime Bercovich e moglie di Ghergo Doblanovich.»

The index knows this man only as «Lunardo» and «Nardo», in 1707 and 1709. **Here the priest writes him out: Leonardo.** And Giacoma is a child of his the index does not have.

That matters for one reason only, and it is worth stating carefully. The Gologorica house's byname is «**detti Leonardi**», and its pedigree runs Leonardus 1697–1773, Leonardus 1766–1848, Leonardus 1847–1917. **A Leonardo de Franceschi is raising a family at Svetvinčenat from 1702.** It is a shared font-name in a family that reuses font-names, and this archive is not going to pretend it is more than that. But it is now a **documented** Leonardo, not an abbreviation.

rows.lab: 4 November 1703 — and here two of them stand together
rows.text:
«**Domenica figlia leg.ma di Piero de Franceschi et di Vittoria sua cons.te**, nata oggi et battezzata di mano del Capell.o Salambat di mia licenza. **Furono compari Nardo Franceschi** et Maria r. q. … Giacomo Gambero.»

**This is the first De Franceschi standing godparent to another De Franceschi in this parish.** Nardo — Leonardo — carries Piero's daughter. Two households of the name in one town, and they are close enough that one christens the other's child. Brothers, or uncle and nephew, on the ordinary reading; the register does not say which, and neither will this page.

rows.lab: 10 May 1707 — and a LUPIERI stands for them
rows.text:
«**Dom.ca figlia leg.ma di M.ro Pietro de Franceschi et Vittoria sua moglie**, nata li 5 d.o… essendo stati Padrini **M.ro Mattio Lupieri**, et Donna Antonia moglie del M.ro Fran.co Mandau.»

Stop on that name. **The Lupieri are the Carnian family of the Canale di Gorto** — of Luint above Ovaro, four kilometres from Mione and Agrons. Brhan devotes a study to their Istrian correspondence; another to the **Stanzia Lupieri** at Sanvincenti, which stood on the road between Svetvinčenat and Canfanaro and is on the 1820 cadastre; a Valentino Lupieri was **podestà of Sanvincenti** in 1824.

So in May 1707 a **Lupieri of the Canale di Gorto stands godfather to a De Franceschi child at Svetvinčenat**. Of every name in these registers, that is the one that ties this household hardest to the valley our own line came out of — not by descent, which nothing here shows, but by **company**. These people were each other's compari.

rows.lab: October 1703 — «S. Mattio de Franceschi», at a twin baptism
rows.text: «Vittoria figlia leg.ma di S. Gieppo Pelizer e di Martina sua moglie, **nata gemella** con la sud.a in d.o parto li 22 sud.o… **Furono compari S. Mattio de Franceschi, et la Sig.ra Madalena Pilastro.**» By 1703 Mattio is *Signor* without qualification.

rows.lab: And a small thing that may settle the count
rows.text: Page 557, 1704: «…li Butcovich **della contrada di [B/R/S]ignano**». That is the **same word** — the same first letter that would not resolve — as the place after «da» in «il Sig.r Conte Lucciani da …» in 1674. Which changes what kind of word it is. **It is not a distant town; it is a contrada of this parish's own territory**, used twice by two different priests. So the count of 1674 was not a visiting grandee from the other side of Istria: he held land here. The Lucciani are an Albona house, and one of them had a holding in the Svetvinčenat country. Inferred

rows.lab: 1706 and 1707 — Nardo becomes the parish's compare
rows.text:
«Mattio figlio leg.o de And.a Saia… Furono P.ni assistenti **M.ro Nardo de Franceschi** e la S.a Andriana…» — 6 September 1706.

«…Comp.ri furono **D. Nardo de Franceschi**, et Elena Machier.» — later in 1707, and now styled **D.**

With the christening of Piero's daughter in 1703 that is three godparent turns for Leonardo in four years. **The role passes down the family**: Nadal holds it in 1666, Anto through 1667–74, Gasparo in 1701, Mattio in 1692 and 1703, Leonardo from 1703. In this parish there is nearly always a De Franceschi being asked.

rows.lab: 15 October 1707 — Piero, twice, and a correction to this page
rows.text:
This archive said three days ago that opening **578 carries no De Franceschi**. It does. The right-hand page opens with one, and the entry was missed. Both of the index's two Pieros have now been found on the film, and they are not what this page first said they were.

**Opening 578, 6 October 1707** — «Piero fig.o leg.mo di M.ro **Nardo de Franceschi** e di Eufemia Jugali, nato li 17 Settembre passato. Fu Battezzato da me medesimo. Assistenti P.ni furono **Martin Salambat** e la **Sig.ra Andriana moglie del Sig.r Can.co Ottavio Quelis**.»

**Opening 579, 15 October 1707** — «Piero fig.o leg.mo di M.ro **Lunardo de Franceschi** et d. Eufemia Jugali, nato li 05 corrente. Fu Battezzato di mia mano. P.ni assistenti **P.re Martino Salambat** … et la **Sig.ra Andriana**…»

Two baptisms, nine days apart, of a boy called Piero, to a mother Eufemia both times and a father written **Nardo** once and **Lunardo** once. The stated births are eighteen days apart, which no mother manages. And **the godparents are the same pair** — Martino Salambat and Andriana Quelis, in the same order, in both entries.

That is the proof. **The duplicate is in the register, not in the index.** The priest entered this child twice and never struck the first, and the top of the second page carries his own dating correction — «15 8bre qui sotto», scribbled above a heading he had first written 16 October. He was already confused about the dates on the page where he wrote it twice.

The index then compounded it. It reads the first birth as 17 September and the second as **25 September** — but the register says «nato li 05 corrente», the 5th of October. Neither index date is the baptism, and one of them is not the birth either.

rows.lab: What this film has given, and what it has not
rows.text:
**Nineteen openings of DGS 005497884 read band by band**: 397, 398, 402, 415, 423, 428, 437, 442, 496, 514, 516, 545, 549, 555, 557, 564, 571, 578, 579. They cover the baptisms of **1666, 1667, 1669, 1671, 1673, 1674, 1688, 1692, 1701, 1702, 1703, 1704, 1706 and 1707**.

**Twenty occurrences of the surname that no index carries.** Sixteen of them are godparent roles — the one category of entry no index transcribes — plus a daughter of Leonardo's the index does not have, and two probable appearances of Marina under her married name.

**Eleven baptisms confirmed word for word. One filiation recovered** — «Ant.o di Franceschi di Piero». **One death dated** — Batta, before July 1688. **Three people added** — Marina, Giacoma, and a probable Maria. **One sex corrected** — Mattia of 1669 is a daughter. **One duplicate found in the register itself** — the two Pieros of October 1707, proved one child by their identical godparents. **One within-family godparent link** — Nardo for Piero's daughter, 1703. And the **Lupieri**.

**One correction to this page, published under the claim it corrects**: the reading that opening 578 held no De Franceschi was wrong. It holds the first of the two Pieros. Reading a page and finding nothing is a claim like any other, and this one failed.

**What the film has not given is an origin.** Not one entry in fourteen years of baptisms says where these people came from. No «da Carnia», no «di Mione», no «q. di Agrons». The Carnian identification of this household still rests entirely on the company it keeps — Spinotti, Fiorencis, Felice, Fabris, Festa, Bergamo, Lupieri — and on Doblanović and Brhan. That is a great deal, and it is not the same thing as a document.

**And the film is 595 images.** Nineteen have been read. The rest hold this parish's marriages and deaths, which is where a place of origin is most likely to be written down, and where Batta's burial and Leonardo's second marriage would be. **This archive has read the pages the index pointed at. It has not read the book.**
